_comments: THE HOURLY ACTIVITY-SYNC ACTION. Fired by the ScheduledJob under metadata/scheduled-jobs/.
DriverClass is a ClassFactory key, not a display name: @RegisterClass(BaseAction,
resolves to, and LoadSyncActivitiesAction() in the server bootstrap is what keeps that
registration from being tree-shaken away. Get either wrong and the action exists in metadata,
is scheduled, fires on time, and does nothing — with no error anywhere.
Downstream apps do not wrap this. They register a BaseActivitySyncExtension (e.g.
Sales.DealLinker) which the engine runs inside the write transaction.
SAFE TO SHIP Active: Graph providers refuse live fetch until an Exchange Application Access
Policy exists, so an hourly run against a Microsoft365 connection writes nothing until a
deployment opts in. A host with no ActivitySyncConnection reports NO_CONNECTIONS.
No sync block — the release push writes that back. primaryKey from uuidgen.

fields.Name: Sync Activities
fields.Description: Pull messages and calendar items for every Active-or-Error activity-sync connection and file the relevant ones as Activities. Downstream apps enrich in-stream via ActivitySyncExtension; they do not own this trigger. Idempotent: re-running over the same window writes nothing new.

fields.Name: Limit
fields.Description: How many items to pull per mailbox per surface per run. MJ's GetMessages contract has no date filter, so a run fetches the most recent N and discards what it has already seen — anything older than the Nth newest message since the last run is missed and never retried.
Every attempted connection completed with no failed items.
At least one connection was attempted and at least one item or surface failed.
The connection list loaded successfully and was empty. Not used when the list failed to load.
The run failed before any connection was attempted (including a failed connection list load), or threw.
